member.name: T:purrTTY.Core.Terminal.TerminalInWorldOptions
member.summary:
Options for an in-world terminal ( / ): a render-to-texture quad drawn in the 3D scene, anchored to a vehicle part or pinned in the camera's view.
The offset/rotation/size members describe the quad in the anchor's frame. For a part anchor they are metres/degrees in the part's local frame; for a billboard / are screen offsets in metres at (and is unused).

member.name: P:purrTTY.Core.Terminal.TerminalInWorldOptions.Cols
member.summary: Grid width in columns (clamped to 8..400). The texture is sized from this and the theme's font cell, so the shell sees about this many columns (a small font on a small grid can yield a few more rows because of a minimum texture size). Default 40.

member.name: P:purrTTY.Core.Terminal.TerminalInWorldOptions.PartInstanceId
member.summary: The game's per-session unique id of the anchor part (Part.InstanceId). When set it is preferred over and is looked up across all vehicles, so it keeps working after the part moves to another vehicle. Not stable across game sessions.

member.name: T:purrTTY.Core.Terminal.TerminalLauncherRegistry
member.summary:
Process-wide rendezvous between purrTTY (which publishes its once initialised and clears it on unload) and other mods (which read it). Because the contract assembly is loaded once and shared, both sides see the same static.
A consumer should treat being null as "terminals unavailable" and subscribe to to attach when purrTTY finishes loading after it, and to detach when purrTTY unloads.
